caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 784 of 1997
lawyer:
M Shamsul Alam, Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner. 
Not represented ----- The Respondents.
parties:
Gazi M Towfic ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Agrani Bank and other ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury J : This civil petition for leave to appeal is against judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 2956 of 1997 summarily rejecting the application impugning the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Money Suit No. 12 of 1995. 

 2. The High Court Division, after having vacated an earlier order rejecting the application as not being pressed, heard the application on merit. The High Court Division held that since Artha Rin Adalat Act was a special law and special provision having been provided in the Act, question of entertaining an application under Article 102 of the Constitution against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat does not arise at all. It was submitted by the Advocate that to prefer an appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat half of the decrial amount had to be deposited before filing the appeal and, as such, it was not an efficacious remedy. This submission was not accepted by the High Court Division which held that since the Artha Rin Adalat Act was a special law and provision having been made for appropriate relief of the aggrieved person, writ application under Article 102 of the Constitution does not lie. The application was therefore summarily rejected. 

 3. The law is now settled that since special provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree. The High Court Division therefore rightly rejected the application summarily.
